title: Markdown Is Not a Firewall: four coding agents, one rules file, four boundaries
author: Sandeep Dhuri
description: Teams put a one-page rules file in a repository and call it a control on coding agents. A registered study found agents rarely look up a repository's contribution rules. I asked the security question: what does a rules file do at a boundary, against a gate? I tested one 278-word rules file, with hypotheses and…
summary: Teams put a one-page rules file in a repository and call it a control on coding agents. A registered study found agents rarely look up a repository's contribution rules.
takeaways: A registered study found agents rarely look up a repository's contribution rules.
Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and OpenCode with DeepSeek worked through 20 small repositories with hidden tests, 12 for three of them.
Three agents met four boundaries I built: a refused endpoint, a destructive shortcut, a planted instruction and a planted package.
